# Configuration reference

Every configuration option these extensions read, with the literal default and
constraints the source gives it. Extracted with a Python parser, so no default is
transcribed by hand.

156 options across 18 modules.

Source: `NebulaOS-klipper-extensions` at `178a0c2`.

**Defaults are never invented.** An option whose default is computed at runtime
rather than written as a literal is shown as `computed` - the source is the only
honest answer there. An option with no default is **required**: Klipper raises an
error if the section omits it.

Section names are the module names, which is how Klipper's `[section]` headers map
to these files.

## Every one of these needs a Klipper restart

**Checked, not assumed.** Every configuration read in this repository happens in a
module's `__init__` or `load_config`, at load time - a scan of all call sites found
no option re-read at runtime. So changing any option below takes effect only after
Klipper restarts, and nothing here can be adjusted live.

On the printer that is **Settings -> Printer -> Restart Klipper**, or
`FIRMWARE_RESTART` from the console. The live adjustments a user can make during a
print - speed, flow, Z offset, pressure advance - are not configuration options and
are not in this file.

## Where the explanations come from

The text below each heading is the module's own header comment, written by its
author. The **Purpose** column is hand-written, by reading the module that uses
the option - not extracted, because this repository carries no inline comments
above its options, and not inferred from the option's name, which would be
invention dressed as documentation.

Where an option is passed straight to a stepper driver register field, the purpose
says so and names the field rather than explaining what the field does. That is
the boundary of what can be established from this source: the driver's own
datasheet is the authority on the field, and paraphrasing it from memory here
would be the same invention in a more convincing costume.

## Some options are accepted and then ignored

A handful of options are read by a module and deliberately **not acted on**. Their
Purpose cell begins *Accepted but not acted on*, and a reader who sets one should
expect nothing to happen.

Two different reasons, both from the source:

- **To stop Klipper refusing to start.** Klipper hard-errors on any option in a
  section that the module never reads. `[z_compensate]` on a real device sets
  `tri_min_hold`, `tri_max_hold` and `speed`, which belonged to a sensitivity
  override removed with PRTouch in Phase 1.8B. They are read and discarded so the
  printer still boots.
- **Because the meaning is unconfirmed.** `type_nozz`, `noz_pos_center`,
  `noz_pos_offset` and `pumpback_mm` are read but unused, and the source explains
  why: `noz_pos_center` is plausibly an XY reference point with nothing confirming
  it, and misapplying it would send the toolhead somewhere unintended;
  `pumpback_mm` is plausibly a pre-wipe retract, and wiring untested E-axis motion
  into a probe and heat sequence was judged not worth the risk on a guess.

That second group is the author choosing to leave a thing visibly unfinished rather
than act on a plausible guess. Documenting them as ordinary settings would undo
that: it would tell a reader these controls work.

Where an option has its own **Purpose**, it was written by reading the module.
Where the cell says *From the source comment*, it is the comment the author left
above that line, quoted. A dash means neither exists - and a dash is the honest
answer, because the alternative is a sentence invented from the option's name.

## `[autotune_tmc]`

Klipper TMC Autotune (autotune_tmc.py)

| Option | Purpose | Type | Default | Constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `extra_hysteresis` | Added to the computed chopper hysteresis before `hstrt` and `hend` are written. The module computes hysteresis from the motor constants, the voltage, the run current, the blank time and `toff`; this is the manual nudge on top, 0-8. | int | `0` (`EXTRA_HYSTERESIS`) | minval 0, maxval 8 |
| `motor` | Which motor this stepper is, by the name of a `[motor_constants <name>]` section (the vendored `motor_database.cfg` supplies them). Required: every tuned value is computed from that motor's electrical constants, so without it there is nothing to tune from. Klipper refuses to start if the name is not defined, and a deprecated alias produces a runtime warning naming the replacement. The KE's stock motors are `creality-42-34` (X/Y) and `creality-42-40` (Z). | string | **required** | - |
| `overvoltage_vth` | *From the source comment:* A zero threshold asserts the overvoltage condition continuously, and values above the TMC2240 absolute maximum cannot protect it in time. Leaving the option unset preserves the driver's hardware default. | float | `none` (`OVERVOLTAGE_VTH`) | above 0.0, maxval 41.0 |
| `pwm_freq_target` | Target chopper frequency in Hz. Sets how many clock cycles one chopper cycle gets, which is what `toff` and `tpfd` are derived from when they are left to the module. The default is per driver type - 55 kHz for the 2130/2208/2209, 20 kHz for the 2240/2660/5160, which the source says run very hot at high frequencies. | float | computed | minval 10000.0, maxval 100000.0 |
| `sedn` | CoolStep current decrement step, written to the driver's `sedn` field. Range 0-3. | int | `2` (`SEDN`) | minval 0, maxval 3 |
| `seimin` | CoolStep minimum-current selector, written to the driver's `seimin` field. 0 or 1. | int | `1` (`SEIMIN`) | minval 0, maxval 1 |
| `semax` | CoolStep upper threshold, written to the driver's `semax` field. Range 0-15. | int | `4` (`SEMAX`) | minval 0, maxval 15 |
| `semin` | CoolStep lower threshold, written to the driver's `semin` field. Range 0-15. | int | `2` (`SEMIN`) | minval 0, maxval 15 |
| `seup` | CoolStep current increment step, written to the driver's `seup` field. Range 0-3. | int | `3` (`SEUP`) | minval 0, maxval 3 |
| `sg4_thrs` | StallGuard4 threshold. Written to `sg4_thrs` on a driver that has StallGuard4 (and `sg4_filt_en` is enabled with it), or to `sgthrs` on a 2209. The default is per driver: 40 generally, but **0 on the TMC2240**, which makes Klipper use the SGT homing path - the one compatible with the SpreadCycle and CoolStep configuration autotune writes. Set it explicitly on a 2240 to opt into SG4 homing. | int | computed | minval 0, maxval 255 |
| `sgt` | StallGuard2 threshold, written to the driver's `sgt` field as part of the CoolStep setup. Range -64 to 63. | int | `1` (`SGT`) | minval -64, maxval 63 |
| `tbl` | Comparator blank time, written to the driver's `tbl` field as an index: 0-3 selects 16/24/32/40 clock cycles on the 2208 and 2209, and 16/24/36/54 on the others. The module overrides a configured `0` to `1` when `toff` ends up at 1, because a 16-cycle blank time does not work in that combination. Also an input to the hysteresis calculation. | int | `1` (`TBL`) | minval 0, maxval 3 |
| `toff` | Slow-decay time, written to the driver's `toff` field. `0`, the default, means **compute it**: the module sizes it so the two slow-decay phases take about half a chopper cycle at `pwm_freq_target`. It is also an input to the hysteresis calculation. | int | `0` (`TOFF`) | minval 0, maxval 15 |
| `tpfd` | Passive fast-decay time, written to the driver's `tpfd` field. Unset by default, which means **compute it** from whatever is left of the chopper cycle after the blank and slow-decay phases. | int | `none` | minval 0, maxval 15 |
| `tuning_goal` | What to optimise for: `silent` (StealthChop at all speeds), `performance` (SpreadCycle at all speeds), `autoswitch` (StealthChop low, SpreadCycle when needed - the module labels this experimental), or `auto`, the default. `auto` resolves at connect time to silent for a motor with holding torque above 0.3 Nm that is not in the module's performance list, and performance otherwise. | string | `auto` (`TUNING_GOAL`) | - |
| `voltage` | The stepper supply voltage, in volts. Not written to the driver: it is an input to the hysteresis, `pwmofs` and `pwmgrad` calculations, so a wrong value makes every derived value wrong. The module raises a config error when a computed PWM value will not fit its 8-bit field and names raising or lowering the voltage as the fix. On a TMC2240 it is also checked against `overvoltage_vth`. | float | `24.0` (`VOLTAGE`) | above 0.0, maxval 60.0 |

## `[nebulaos_power_loss_recovery]`

NebulaOS's own power-loss recovery extra (Phase 1.9B), built entirely on public/mainline Klipper interfaces.

Tested by `extras/test_nebulaos_power_loss_recovery.py`.

| Option | Purpose | Type | Default | Constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `checkpoint_interval` | Seconds between checkpoints during a print. Shorter loses less to a power cut and writes more often. | float | `5.0` (`DEFAULT_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL`) | above 0.0 |
| `eeprom_path` | Sysfs path of the small EEPROM holding the durable checkpoint record - the only thing trusted as proof that a checkpoint fully landed. | string | `/sys/bus/i2c/devices/2-0050/eeprom` (`DEFAULT_EEPROM_PATH`) | - |
| `min_z_for_start` | Height below which no checkpoint is taken, so a cut in the first moments of a print does not offer a useless recovery. | float | `0.6` (`DEFAULT_MIN_Z_FOR_START`) | minval 0.0 |
| `physical_resume` | Whether a resume actually restarts printing. **Off by default**: with it off, NEBULAOS_PLR_RESUME restores state only. The source records that it stays off until it has passed a supervised power-cut test print on the machine in question. | bool | `false` | - |
| `poll_interval` | Seconds between checks of print state while deciding whether to checkpoint. | float | `0.75` (`DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL`) | above 0.0 |
| `prime_length` | Millimetres of filament extruded at the park position during a physical resume, after the nozzle has reached temperature and before the toolhead returns to the print. It primes away the ooze and the gap left by the power cut, as `G1 E<prime_length> F300` in relative extrusion, and the extruder position is restored afterwards so the resumed file's E coordinates still line up. `0` disables the prime; the maximum is 50. | float | `8.0` (`DEFAULT_PRIME_LENGTH`) | minval 0.0, maxval 50.0 |
| `resume_z_lift` | How far to lift Z before moving back to the interrupted position, so the nozzle does not drag across the part. | float | `5.0` (`DEFAULT_RESUME_Z_LIFT`) | minval 1.0, maxval 20.0 |
| `sidecar_dir` | Directory for the larger JSON checkpoint files, written and fsynced before the EEPROM record so a power cut cannot leave the two disagreeing. | string | `/usr/data/nebulaos/printer_data/plr` (`DEFAULT_SIDECAR_DIR`) | - |
| `timelapse_frame_path` | Directory moonraker-timelapse keeps its frames in. Set it to preserve a timelapse across a power cut: on resume the frames from before the cut are set aside, and _NEBULAOS_PLR_TIMELAPSE_MERGE puts them back in front, renumbered without a gap, before Moonraker renders. Empty disables the handling, and the timelapse is lost on resume. | string | `""` | - |

| `contact_speed` | Speed of the slow downward move that makes contact. Slower reads the touch more precisely. | float | `2.0` | minval 0.1, maxval 10.0 |
| `force_safety_limit` | Force above which the probe aborts, so a runaway contact stops rather than pressing harder. | float | `2000.0` | minval 100.0, maxval 10000.0 |

Never in an image-owned cfg (configfile include conflict). G99: superseded by the automatic check's reference (state... | int | `none` | - |
| `raw_settle_time` | *From the source comment:* Run 15 (ke-dev compare, 2026-10-20): right after earlier touches (~270 g each) and travel moves, the bed is still settling - drift -865 counts/s, p2p 4445 for the first window. Settling (drift or noise above the profile) is measured again in consecutive windows for up to raw_settle_time; real... | float | `5.0` | minval 0.3, maxval 30.0 |
| `retract_dist` | How far to lift after a touch before the next sample. | float | `2.0` | minval 0.5, maxval 10.0 |
| `retract_speed` | Speed of that lift. | float | `10.0` | minval 1.0, maxval 50.0 |

## `[nozzle_clear]`

Native nozzle-wipe routine using upstream Klipper's load-cell probe

| Option | Purpose | Type | Default | Constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bed_max_err` | Allowance for bed position error. Also serves as the fallback hover height when vs_start_z_pos is unset. | float | `5` | minval 1 |
| `clr_noz_len_x` | Width of the wipe pad area, within which the two probe points are randomised. | float | `1.0` | minval 1 |
| `clr_noz_len_y` | Depth of the wipe pad area. | float | `1.0` | minval 1 |
| `clr_noz_start_x` | X corner where the wipe pad area starts. The default of 0 is deliberate: the pad sits partly off the near edge of the bed's own X origin. | float | `0.0` | minval -50, maxval 1000 |
| `clr_noz_start_y` | Y corner where the wipe pad area starts. | float | `0.0` | minval 0, maxval 1000 |
| `clr_xy_spd` | Speed of the wiping move itself - slow, because it is a dragging contact. | float | `2.0` | minval 0.1 |
| `g29_down_min_z` | Lowest Z the downward probing move is allowed to reach, bounding the search. | float | `25` | minval 1 |
| `pa_clr_dis_mm_x` | How far the nozzle is dragged along X during the wipe. | float | `30` | minval -100, maxval 100 |
| `pa_clr_dis_mm_y` | How far the nozzle is dragged along Y during the wipe. Zero means a straight X-only wipe. | float | `0` | minval -100, maxval 100 |
| `pa_clr_down_mm` | How far below the probed pad surface the nozzle presses while wiping. Negative presses into the pad, which is what makes the wipe contact. | float | `-0.15` | minval -1, maxval 1 |
| `pr_clear_probe_cnt` | How many probe samples must agree at each of the two wipe-pad points before the wipe proceeds. | int | `3` | minval 1 |
| `rdy_xy_spd` | Travel speed used to get to the pad, much faster than the wipe. | float | `200` | minval 1 |
| `vs_start_z_pos` | Hover height above the pad before probing starts. Defaults to bed_max_err, a dual use that predates this option. | float | `bed_max_err` | - |

Per-print auto-Z-offset orchestration, host-side Klipper extra

| Option | Purpose | Type | Default | Constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bed_add_temp` | *From the source comment:* bed_add_temp (real key): the bed temperature for the nozzle-wipe - the wipe heats the bed to the higher of its current target and this value, clamped to [heater_bed] max_temp (wipe_bed_temp() above; it used to be added to the target, which asked for 125 C after a 65 C PID target).... | float | `0` | minval -20, maxval 100 |
| `bl_offset` | X and Y offset of the BLTouch from the nozzle, as two numbers. | float list | `(0.0, 0.0)` | - |
| `hot_end_temp` | *From the source comment:* hot_end_temp (real key): final nozzle temp after the wipe - threaded through to prtouch_nozzle.clear_nozzle()'s hot_end_temp param. | float | `none` | minval 80, maxval 300 |
| `hot_rub_temp` | Nozzle temperature held while the nozzle is rubbed against the pad. | float | `180` | minval 80, maxval 300 |
| `hot_start_temp` | Nozzle temperature to reach before the wipe sequence begins. | float | `150` | minval 80, maxval 200 |
| `max_offset_correction_mm` | *From the source comment:* max_offset_correction_mm (2026-08-09 hardening mission, new): a sanity ceiling on the magnitude of a candidate correction before it's ever applied as a live offset - this command is documented (module docstring) as a per-print THERMAL/WEAR FINE-TUNE, not a full re-leveling; a multi-millimeter... | float | `2.0` | minval 0.1, maxval 10.0 |
| `noz_pos_center` | **Accepted but not acted on.** The source records this as plausibly another XY reference point, with nothing confirming it - and notes that misapplying it would send the toolhead somewhere unintended. Read, not used, flagged rather than silently dropped. | float list | `(0.0, 0.0)` | - |
| `noz_pos_offset` | **Accepted but not acted on.** As noz_pos_center: plausibly an XY reference, unconfirmed, deliberately not acted on. | float list | `(0.0, 0.0)` | - |
| `persist_offset` | *From the source comment:* Opt-in permanent persistence (see module docstring) - off by default. | bool | `false` | - |
| `pr_probe_cnt` | *From the source comment:* pr_probe_cnt (real key): probe-agreement count for this command's own touch, distinct from clear_nozzle()'s own pr_clear_probe_cnt (read in prtouch_nozzle.py). | int | `3` | minval 1 |
| `pumpback_mm` | **Accepted but not acted on.** The source records this as plausibly a pre-wipe retract, unconfirmed, and judges that wiring untested E-axis motion into a probe and heat sequence is not worth the risk on a guess. | float | `0.0` | - |
| `save_config_command` | G-code command used to persist the offset when persist_offset is on. Normally Klipper's own SAVE_CONFIG. | string | `SAVE_CONFIG` | - |
| `speed` | **Accepted but not acted on.** As tri_min_hold - read, unused, present because the real device sets it (5). | float | `none` | minval 0.1 |
| `tri_expand_mm` | *From the source comment:* tri_expand_mm (real key): no source exists for z_compensate_wrapper.so (see module docstring), so this is an inference, not a confirmed port - applied as a fixed additive correction to the Z_OFFSET_CALIBRATION measurement, on the theory that it accounts for a systematic gap between the load... | float | `0.0` | - |
| `tri_max_hold` | **Accepted but not acted on.** As tri_min_hold - read, unused, present because the real device sets it (2000). | int | `none` | - |
| `tri_min_hold` | **Accepted but not acted on.** Read only so Klipper does not refuse to start: the real device's [z_compensate] section sets it (1400), and Klipper hard-errors on any section option that is never read. The sensitivity-override mechanism it belonged to was removed with PRTouch in Phase 1.8B, and the native probe backend has no equivalent. | int | `none` | - |
| `type_nozz` | **Accepted but not acted on.** The source records its meaning as unknown. Read so Klipper starts; nothing uses the value. | int | `0` | - |
| `vs_start_z_pos` | *From the source comment:* vs_start_z_pos (real key, replaces the old Klipper-only z_offset_hover_height default): hover height before the (unregistered, see header) Z_OFFSET_CALIBRATION touch, and passed through to clear_nozzle() for its own two wipe-pad touches. | float | `5` | minval 1, maxval 50 |
| `z_offset_down_min_z` | Lowest Z the downward probing move may reach during Z offset calibration. | float | `10` | minval 1, maxval 50 |
